review.tagline: Graph-based RAG framework with a REST API server and web UI
review.summary: LightRAG indexes documents into a knowledge graph plus vector embeddings and answers queries with dual-level (entity and concept) retrieval. It ships as a Python library and as lightrag-server, which provides a REST API and a web UI for inserting, querying and visualizing the graph. It supports incremental updates, document deletion with graph rebuild, reranking, and several parsing and chunking options.
review.audience: Engineers building graph-based document Q&A over large corpora
strengths: Document deletion rebuilds affected graph entries from the LLM cache; inserts are incremental
Storage backends include PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB and OpenSearch, plus local file stores
Parsers: MinerU, Docling and a native engine; four chunking strategies
Setup wizard generates .env and compose files; RAGAS evaluation and Langfuse tracing supported
weaknesses: Default in-memory/file stores are stated as not for production
Server binds to 0.0.0.0 and endpoints are public until auth is set in .env
Graph extraction needs LLM calls at index time; RAM and GPU needs are unstated
Optional features need extra steps: spaCy models for smart_heading, libcairo for SVG
needs: Needs LLM provider, embedding model, PostgreSQL (recommended for production), Neo4j (optional), MongoDB (optional), OpenSearch (optional), MinerU or Docling (optional)
Models: LLMs configured via .env, open-source LLMs such as Qwen3-30B-A3B, rerankers
